product: Mitapivat (PYRUKYND/AQVESME), an oral pyruvate kinase activator, approved for PK deficiency (2022) and thalassemia (U.S. 2025; EU 2026-05-22); sickle cell sNDA under review (2026-07-07). Pipeline: AG-236 in polycythemia vera, AG-181 in PKU, and cevidoplenib for ITP (2026-07-30).
demand: Volume and launch driven. U.S. net revenue of $40.9M in Q2 2026 came from the new AQVESME thalassemia launch (late January 2026) with 442 prescriptions by 2026-06-30; ex-U.S. revenue was $3.8M on EU and GCC uptake. No price increases were disclosed (2026-07-30, investor.agios.com).
pricing_power: Gross margin is ~93% (cost of sales $3.0M vs $44.7M Q2 2026), so collapse would come from R&D/SG&A, not COGS: R&D was $100.8M and SG&A $51.5M in Q2 2026, including a $25M Oscotec upfront; net loss $100.7M (2026-07-30, investor.agios.com).
competition: not found. No Chinese or generic low-cost mitapivat substitute identified; PYRUKYND/AQVESME are patented first-in-class oral PK activators. In sickle cell the nearer substitutes are gene therapies and rival PK activators rather than low-cost generics (2026-07-07, investor.agios.com).
market_strategy: CEO Brian Goff (2026-07-30, investor.agios.com) cited strong commercial momentum, pipeline diversification, and strategic portfolio discipline. Dated commitments: advance cevidoplenib into Phase 3 for ITP in H1 2028; start AG-236 Phase 2 in polycythemia vera in H2 2026; report AG-181 Phase 1b data in H2 2026.
bull: Mitapivat Q2 2026 revenue $44.7M vs $12.5M, cash $964.8M, 93% gross margin, and a dated FDA PDUFA 2026-11-01 for sickle cell with Priority Review; ENERGIZE-T Phase 3 published in The Lancet 2026-09-11.
bear: Momentum negative (21d -4.2%, 63d -14.0%), tebapivat discontinued 2026-07-21, net loss $100.7M, and the sickle cell case rests on one binary 2026-11-01 FDA decision; §17 target upside is perverse, not a reason to buy.
falsifier: FDA issues a CRL or delays the mitapivat sickle cell sNDA past the 2026-11-01 PDUFA date.
web_what_changed_30_90d: In the last 30 days, ENERGIZE-T Phase 3 thalassemia data were published in The Lancet (2026-09-11, @AgiosPharma). In the last 90 days: FDA granted Priority Review to mitapivat's sickle cell sNDA, PDUFA 2026-11-01 (2026-07-07); tebapivat was discontinued in sickle cell (2026-07-21); Q2 2026 mitapivat revenue was $44.7M vs $12.5M (2026-07-30).
web_true_now_not_modelled: Mitapivat worldwide net revenue reached $44.7M in Q2 2026 versus $12.5M in Q2 2025, aided by the AQVESME U.S. thalassemia launch with 442 cumulative prescriptions as of 2026-06-30; cash was $964.8M (2026-07-30). Tebapivat is fully discontinued, so the Nov 1 2026 sickle cell decision is the dominant single catalyst.
web_demand_product: Mitapivat (PYRUKYND/AQVESME), an oral pyruvate kinase activator, approved for PK deficiency (2022) and thalassemia (U.S. 2025; EU 2026-05-22); sickle cell sNDA under review (2026-07-07). Pipeline: AG-236 in polycythemia vera, AG-181 in PKU, and cevidoplenib for ITP (2026-07-30).
web_price_volume_mix: Volume and launch driven. U.S. net revenue of $40.9M in Q2 2026 came from the new AQVESME thalassemia launch (late January 2026) with 442 prescriptions by 2026-06-30; ex-U.S. revenue was $3.8M on EU and GCC uptake. No price increases were disclosed (2026-07-30, investor.agios.com).
web_bottleneck: Regulatory plus launch logistics. The U.S. sickle cell opportunity hinges on FDA accelerated approval by the 2026-11-01 PDUFA with the REIGNITE confirmatory Phase 3 underway (first patient dosed) (2026-07-07, 2026-07-30). AQVESME uptake is gated by REMS-certified prescribers (442 scripts by 2026-06-30).
web_who_benefits_next: On approval (2026-11-01), Agios and its shareholders, REMS-certified U.S. prescribers, and sickle cell patients benefit; EU and GCC approvals extend reach (2026-07-30). Second-order: contract manufacturers and the oral PK-activator class, as PK activation is clinically validated in sickle cell by tebapivat data (2026-07-21).
web_who_loses: Sickle cell gene therapies and competing disease-modifiers lose share to an oral option: Vertex/CRISPR Casgevy, bluebird bio Lyfgenia, Novartis crizanlizumab, Pfizer voxelotor (withdrawn), and Agios' own tebapivat, discontinued in SCD 2026-07-21 (prior card 2026-09-25; investor.agios.com 2026-07-30).
web_margin_collapse_risk: Gross margin is ~93% (cost of sales $3.0M vs $44.7M Q2 2026), so collapse would come from R&D/SG&A, not COGS: R&D was $100.8M and SG&A $51.5M in Q2 2026, including a $25M Oscotec upfront; net loss $100.7M (2026-07-30, investor.agios.com).
web_low_cost_substitute: not found. No Chinese or generic low-cost mitapivat substitute identified; PYRUKYND/AQVESME are patented first-in-class oral PK activators. In sickle cell the nearer substitutes are gene therapies and rival PK activators rather than low-cost generics (2026-07-07, investor.agios.com).
web_ceo_promised: CEO Brian Goff (2026-07-30, investor.agios.com) cited strong commercial momentum, pipeline diversification, and strategic portfolio discipline. Dated commitments: advance cevidoplenib into Phase 3 for ITP in H1 2028; start AG-236 Phase 2 in polycythemia vera in H2 2026; report AG-181 Phase 1b data in H2 2026.
web_did_they_deliver: Yes on filings. Agios submitted the sickle cell sNDA (2026-05-12) and FDA granted Priority Review with PDUFA 2026-11-01 (2026-07-07); RISE UP Phase 3 was presented at EHA (2026-06-13) and ENERGIZE-T data published (2026-09-11). It also disclosed negative tebapivat results and discontinued that program (2026-07-21).
web_what_would_falsify: FDA issues a CRL or delays the mitapivat sickle cell sNDA past the 2026-11-01 PDUFA date, approves without REIGNITE confirmatory trial underway, or a safety CRL; also a quarterly mitapivat revenue shortfall versus the $44.7M Q2 2026 base, or failure to start AG-236 Phase 2 in H2 2026 (2026-07-07, 2026-07-30).
